ed-getting-hired-l01.q: A posting reads "Patient Care Technician II - Emergency Services, freestanding emergency department." What does the word freestanding tell you about the work?
choices: There are no inpatient beds, so patients are stabilized and then transferred or discharged, and one or two techs do everything
It is a trauma center, so the tech mostly assists residents
It is an urgent care, so no critical patients arrive
It is a training site, so the tech has no patient contact
ed-getting-hired-l01.why: A freestanding ED is a satellite emergency department with no hospital attached. It stabilizes and then moves the patient out. Staffing is thin, so the tech does the whole range of tasks. Acuity averages lower, but a heart attack still walks in the door.

ed-getting-hired-l01.q: A system posts "Paramedic - ED" at about six dollars an hour above its ED tech line. You hold a New Jersey EMT certification. What is the correct move?
choices: Apply and explain that EMT is close enough to paramedic
Apply to the ED tech postings, because paramedic is a separate certification with a wider scope
Apply to both and let the recruiter sort it out
Ask the recruiter to waive the paramedic requirement based on the BLS card
ed-getting-hired-l01.why: Paramedic is a different, higher certification with a wider scope of practice, not a senior version of EMT. Applying without it burns your record with that system. Applying to both wastes the recruiter's time. Certification requirements are verified, not waived.

ed-getting-hired-l02.q: You receive the third and final dose of the hepatitis B series today. When is the surface antibody titer drawn?
choices: The same day, before you leave
Within one week
1 to 2 months after the last dose
One year later at the annual health visit
ed-getting-hired-l02.why: The titer is drawn 1 to 2 months after the final dose, because antibody levels need time to rise. Drawing it the same day or within a week gives an uninterpretable result. Waiting a year delays clearance and may miss a non-responder who needs a repeat series.

ed-getting-hired-l02.q: Your start date is in eleven days and you can get to employee health only once. TB screening has not been done. Which test fits the time you have?
choices: A two-step tuberculin skin test
A chest x-ray instead of any screening
An IGRA blood test such as QuantiFERON, which needs one visit
Nothing; TB screening is done after the first 90 days
ed-getting-hired-l02.why: An IGRA such as QuantiFERON is a single blood draw at one visit. The two-step skin test requires four visits over 1 to 3 weeks, which does not fit. A chest x-ray is a follow-up to a positive screen, not a screen. TB clearance is a pre-start contingency, not a post-hire task.

ed-getting-hired-l03.q: A posting reads "0.5 FTE, evenings." How many hours a week is that, and what does it mean for benefits?
choices: 20 hours a week, and benefits eligibility is borderline because the threshold is usually about 0.5 to 0.6 FTE and is set by the system
20 hours a week, and benefits are guaranteed because any FTE number means benefits
30 hours a week, and benefits are guaranteed
40 hours a week at half pay, with no benefits
ed-getting-hired-l03.why: 1.0 FTE is 40 hours, so 0.5 is 20. Benefits eligibility commonly starts near 0.5 to 0.6 FTE, but the threshold is written by each system, so you read the posting rather than assume. An FTE number by itself guarantees nothing, and 0.5 FTE is not full-time hours at half pay.

ed-getting-hired-l03.q: An offer includes a `$5,000` sign-on bonus. What is the detail you must confirm in writing before you accept?
choices: Whether the bonus counts toward your FTE
Whether the bonus is paid before the drug screen
Whether the bonus raises your step on the pay grid
The payback clause: how much you owe if you leave inside 12 or 24 months
ed-getting-hired-l03.why: Sign-on bonuses almost always carry a repayment obligation tied to a service period of 12 or 24 months. That clause, not the headline number, decides what the bonus is worth. A bonus is a one-time payment, so it does not touch FTE or the step grid, and nothing contingent is paid before the screens clear.

ed-getting-hired-l04.q: The posting says "point-of-care testing." Your resume says "bedside lab tests." What should you do?
choices: Leave it; the manager will understand the meaning
Change the resume to say point-of-care testing, the posting's exact words
Write both phrases in the same bullet to cover either search
Delete the line because the phrasing is ambiguous
ed-getting-hired-l04.why: Applicant tracking software matches strings, not meaning, so the posting's exact vocabulary is what gets found. The manager never sees the resume the parser drops. Stuffing both phrasings reads as padded, and deleting a real skill costs you the match entirely.

ed-getting-hired-l04.q: You completed a phlebotomy course but have not yet passed the NHA CPT exam. What belongs on the resume?
choices: List it as "NHA CPT certified" because the course is finished
List it as "CPT (in progress)" under Certifications with no exam date
State the course completed and the exam date scheduled, and do not claim the certification
Leave phlebotomy off entirely until the card arrives
ed-getting-hired-l04.why: Credentials are verified, and claiming one you do not hold ends the application permanently. Stating the completed course and a scheduled exam is both true and useful. A vague "in progress" with no date is weak, and omitting real training throws away a preferred qualification.

ed-getting-hired-l05.q: The panel interview ends at 3 p.m. Tuesday. What is the correct first action?
choices: Send a three- to five-sentence thank-you email to each interviewer within 24 hours, naming one specific thing from the conversation
Wait a week so you do not seem eager, then email the recruiter
Call the manager that evening to ask whether you got it
Send one thank-you to the recruiter and let her forward it
ed-getting-hired-l05.why: A short, specific thank-you inside 24 hours to every interviewer is rare enough to be remembered. Waiting a week loses the moment. A same-day phone call to the manager reads as pressure. A forwarded note does not reach the people who scored you.

ed-getting-hired-l05.q: A posting you want went live yesterday on the hospital's career site and is also listed on three job boards. What is the best move?
choices: Apply on the job board with the fastest one-click submission
Apply on all four so your name appears repeatedly
Wait a week so the first wave of applicants clears
Apply on the hospital's own portal inside 72 hours of the posting date and save the requisition number
ed-getting-hired-l05.why: Job boards mostly repost and route you back to the portal anyway, so applying at the source keeps one clean record and gets you the requisition number. Many requisitions are reviewed in batches and close early, so speed matters. Duplicate applications clutter your file rather than raise your odds.

ed-getting-hired-l06.q: A candidate ends a STAR answer with "and after that things went a lot more smoothly." What is missing?
choices: The situation, which should have opened the answer
The result, which should be one sentence with a number or a concrete outcome
The task, which should have been two or three sentences
Nothing; a qualitative ending is the goal
ed-getting-hired-l06.why: The R in STAR is one sentence carrying a number or a specific outcome, which is what makes the story verifiable. "Things went more smoothly" is unmeasurable. The situation and task are each one sentence and clearly were present; the action is the part that gets three or four sentences.

ed-getting-hired-l06.q: Asked "where do you see yourself in five years," an ED tech candidate who plans to apply to PA school should:
choices: Say he intends to stay an ED tech indefinitely
Refuse the question as none of the panel's business
Say PA school is the plan and that this role is a step toward it, without saying more about the job itself
Say PA school is the goal, then commit concretely to doing this job well now and name what he wants to master here
ed-getting-hired-l06.why: An honest PA-school answer usually helps, because the panel has seen the path many times. What sinks candidates is making the department sound like a waiting room, which is exactly the version that mentions only the next step. A false plan to stay forever is easy to see through, and refusing the question reads as evasive.

ed-getting-hired-l07.q: Which question should you keep out of a first interview even though it is a reasonable thing to want to know?
choices: How soon can I use paid time off, and what happened to the last person in this role
What does orientation look like and how long is the precepted period
What is the tech-to-patient ratio on a typical night
What separates a tech who does well here from one who struggles
ed-getting-hired-l07.why: Time off and the previous jobholder are fair questions that are read as warning signs at the first interview, so they wait until an offer is in hand. Orientation length, staffing ratio, and what success looks like all mark you as someone thinking about the work.

ed-getting-hired-l07.q: You are set up for a video panel interview at 10 a.m. Which arrangement is correct?
choices: Sit with a window behind you for natural light and join at 10 a.m. exactly
Camera at eye level, light source in front of you, plain background, join 10 minutes early to test audio, and look at the lens when you speak
Camera below eye level on a laptop in your lap, with the screen faces to look at while answering
Join by phone audio only so connection problems cannot interrupt you
ed-getting-hired-l07.why: Light in front and a camera at eye level make you legible; a window behind turns you into a silhouette. Joining ten minutes early catches audio problems before they cost you. Looking at the lens reads as eye contact, while looking at the faces on screen does not. Dropping to audio only throws away the interview's whole visual half.

ed-getting-hired-l08.q: You are 60 days into the job. What does the 90-day probationary period mean for you right now?
choices: You are paid at a reduced training rate until day 90
You cannot be scheduled for nights or weekends yet
The usual progressive discipline process does not yet apply, so employment can end without it
Your competency checklist cannot be signed until day 90
ed-getting-hired-l08.why: During probation the step-by-step discipline process that normally protects an employee has not attached yet, which is why the first three months count double. Pay, scheduling, and competency sign-offs are separate matters; checklist lines are signed as you demonstrate each skill, often well before day 90.

ed-getting-hired-l08.q: Mid-shift you realize you scanned and labeled a blood tube at the bedside with the wrong patient's label. What is the first action?
choices: Tell the patient's nurse immediately
Quietly pull the tube out of the lab tube system and redraw it
Finish the assignment and mention it at handoff
Write the correct name on the label by hand and send it
ed-getting-hired-l08.why: Telling the nurse immediately is what lets the specimen be stopped and a result acted on before it reaches the wrong chart. Delay and concealment, not the mistake itself, are what end jobs. Never hand-alter a label, and never quietly fix a labeling error alone, because the record of what happened is part of patient safety.

ed-getting-hired-l09.q: You have 50 minutes before leaving for a `1900` shift and want to nap. What is the best choice?
choices: Sleep the full 50 minutes for maximum rest
Sleep 20 to 30 minutes, because 45 to 60 minutes wakes you out of deep sleep feeling worse
Skip the nap and take caffeine instead, since any nap causes grogginess
Sleep 90 minutes and leave late
ed-getting-hired-l09.why: A 20 to 30 minute nap ends before deep sleep, so you wake sharp. A 45 to 60 minute nap is the worst window, because it wakes you mid deep sleep. A full 90-minute cycle is fine when you have room, but not at the cost of being late. A pre-shift nap is the highest-yield habit on nights, so skipping it is not the answer.

ed-getting-hired-l09.q: A tuition reimbursement program lists `$5,250` per year. Why does that exact figure appear so often?
choices: It is the average cost of a semester of prerequisites
It is a New Jersey statutory maximum for hospital benefits
It is the IRS limit on employer education assistance that is not taxed as income
It is the amount a union contract sets for allied health workers
ed-getting-hired-l09.why: `$5,250` is the federal limit on educational assistance an employer can provide without it being taxed as the employee's income, which is why so many programs stop precisely there. It is not a tuition estimate, a state statute, or a union figure, and programs commonly start lower, around `$2,500`.

ed-getting-hired-l10.q: You have 2,400 hours as an ED tech and 30 hours of PA shadowing. How do most applications treat the 30 hours?
choices: They are added to the 2,400 as patient care experience
They are entered separately as shadowing, which most programs want at roughly 20 to 40 hours
They count as healthcare experience only if paid
They are not reported because they overlap your employment
ed-getting-hired-l10.why: Shadowing is observation, so it is logged in its own category and commonly expected at 20 to 40 hours. Rolling it into paid patient care hours misstates the application, which is verified. Shadowing is unpaid by definition, and it is reported even when it happens in the department where you work.

ed-getting-hired-l10.q: Your ED manager is leaving next month for another health system. Before her last day, what matters most for your future PA application?
choices: Ask her to write the letter of recommendation now, before you have worked a full year
Ask for a copy of your competency checklist
Ask her to raise your step on the pay grid as a parting favor
Get her personal email and cell number, and confirm your job title, start date, and average hours per week
ed-getting-hired-l10.why: The application asks for a supervisor's contact information and verifies dates and hours, and reconstructing that from memory after a manager has moved systems is the most avoidable problem in the process. A strong letter is asked for at 12 months or more of working together. The checklist and the pay grid do not appear on the application.

quiz.q: A career site search for "emergency technician" returns nothing, but the system has a busy 60-bed emergency department. Which search strategy is most likely to surface the opening?
choices: Search the words "emergency" and "technician" separately, and also try patient care technician, clinical associate, clinical care partner, and emergency care technician
Search only for "ED tech" and check back weekly
Call the ED charge nurse and ask her to post a job
Apply to any open nursing assistant role and request a transfer later
quiz.why: The same job is posted under at least six titles, and many postings never contain the word tech, so searching both words separately plus each title variant is what finds it. Repeating one failed search changes nothing. Charge nurses do not create requisitions, and transferring in after taking an unrelated role is slower and far less certain than applying to the real posting.

quiz.q: A new EMT wants the fastest possible progression to drawing blood, running 12-leads, and applying splints personally rather than watching. Which department type best fits?
choices: An academic Level I trauma center, because volume is highest
A community ED, where a small permanent crew means techs own more of the procedural work
A freestanding ED, because acuity is lowest
Any department, because tech scope is set nationally
quiz.why: Community EDs run on a small permanent crew, so techs there typically own blood draws, EKGs, splints, and catheters. At an academic Level I center residents want the procedures, so the tech personally does fewer of them despite the volume. Low acuity is not the same as more procedures. Scope is set by the department, not nationally.

quiz.q: Two candidates compare EDs. One wants the strongest teaching environment for a future PA application. Which feature of an academic Level I trauma center matters most for that goal?
choices: It pays the highest base rate in the region
It has the fewest written protocols, so staff improvise
Residents and fellows are learning on the floor, so explaining is already the culture
Techs there perform the widest range of procedures
quiz.why: The teaching value comes from working among people whose job includes being taught and explaining, which makes questions normal. Academic centers have more written protocol, not less. Techs at those centers generally perform fewer procedures than community ED techs, and pay does not track trauma level reliably.

quiz.q: An applicant living in Camden County rules out every Philadelphia posting on principle. What is the practical problem with that rule?
choices: Pennsylvania hospitals cannot legally hire New Jersey residents
Philadelphia systems routinely hire New Jersey residents, so the rule discards a large share of nearby openings
A New Jersey EMT certification is invalid at a Pennsylvania hospital tech job
Commuting across the bridge disqualifies you from New Jersey licensure
quiz.why: Applying across the bridge is normal and Philadelphia systems hire New Jersey residents constantly, so an automatic exclusion throws away real openings. The honest tradeoff is the drive itself, especially after a night shift. There is no residency bar, and working in Pennsylvania does not affect New Jersey certification.

quiz.q: During an interview a candidate asks, "What does the tech actually do here?" and the manager answers that techs do vitals and transport only, with no needles. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The manager is testing whether the candidate will push back
The answer is temporary and will change once the candidate is hired
This is a real and accurate description of scope at this department, which is set locally rather than by title
The department is out of compliance with state rules on tech scope
quiz.why: Tech scope is set by the department, so one hospital's tech starts IVs while another four miles away does not let techs touch a needle, and the manager's answer is simply the truth about this building. Nothing here is a test or a temporary condition, and there is no state rule requiring techs to draw blood.

quiz.q: A candidate holds a card from a weekend course titled "CPR Certified - Adult, Child, Infant" taken entirely online. Employee health rejects it. What satisfies the requirement?
choices: An American Heart Association BLS Provider card, including blended HeartCode with an in-person skills session, valid 2 years
The same online card plus a signed letter from the course provider
Any CPR card less than 6 months old
An ACLS card only, because it supersedes BLS
quiz.why: Hospitals require a healthcare-provider BLS card with a hands-on skills check, and AHA BLS Provider is the standard; blended HeartCode qualifies once the in-person skills session is complete. A layperson card is not upgraded by a letter or by being recent. ACLS is a separate course and does not replace the BLS requirement at hire.

quiz.q: An applicant decides today that he wants an ED tech job and hopes to start in about four months. Which item has the longest lead time and should begin immediately?
choices: The N95 respirator fit test
The BLS Provider course
The hepatitis B series, given at 0, 1, and 6 months with a titer 1 to 2 months after the last dose
The 10-panel drug screen
quiz.why: The hepatitis B series plus its titer takes roughly 7 to 8 months, which is by far the longest pole and the only item on this list that cannot be compressed. A fit test is about 20 minutes, BLS is one day, and the drug screen happens within 24 to 72 hours of an offer and cannot be done early.

quiz.q: New Jersey does not license phlebotomists. Why does a candidate still benefit from the NHA CPT certificate?
choices: It is legally required for hospital employment in New Jersey
It signals to a manager that she does not have to teach you to draw blood, and it often bumps your starting step
It allows the tech to start peripheral IVs without department sign-off
It replaces the EMT certification on most postings
quiz.why: The value is practical rather than legal: the certificate tells a hiring manager the training cost is already paid, and many systems credit it on the step grid. It is not required, it does not expand scope to IV starts, which still require department sign-off, and it does not substitute for EMT certification.

quiz.q: A phlebotomy program tells a student he cannot be signed off until he completes a set number of successful sticks. Which figure is typical?
choices: 5 venipunctures and 5 capillary sticks
100 venipunctures and 50 capillary sticks
10 venipunctures only, with no capillary requirement
30 venipunctures and 10 capillary sticks
quiz.why: Programs commonly require about 30 successful venipunctures and 10 capillary sticks before sign-off, which is enough repetition to make the skill reliable. Five of each is too few to certify competence, 100 and 50 is a clinical-rotation volume no certificate course carries, and capillary technique is a separate skill that is always included.

quiz.q: An applicant lists a job as running "2023 to 2024" on the application because he cannot recall exact months. The background check flags it. Why does this matter more than most applicants expect?
choices: Employment dates are verified against the employer's records, and discrepancies can cancel a contingent offer
Year-only entries are illegal on hospital applications
The system assumes any gap means termination for cause
It automatically triggers fingerprinting
quiz.why: Every offer is contingent, and background checks verify each job and school you list, so date mismatches read as inaccuracy on a document you signed. Year-only reporting is not illegal but it invites the mismatch. Gaps are not presumed to be firings, and fingerprinting is a system policy rather than a penalty.

quiz.q: Which statement about the pre-employment drug screen is accurate for a New Jersey hospital applicant?
choices: Legalization in New Jersey means a cannabis result cannot affect a hospital offer
Hospitals holding federal contracts and safety-sensitive employers still test and still rescind offers, so legalization is not protection for a pre-employment screen
Only applicants for medication-handling roles are screened
The screen is run after 90 days of employment rather than before hire
quiz.why: New Jersey law limits some employer actions based on a cannabis test alone, but federal contractors and safety-sensitive employers still screen and still withdraw offers, so an applicant should not treat legalization as cover. Screening is standard for the whole workforce, and it is a pre-start contingency, usually within 24 to 72 hours of the offer.

quiz.q: A posting reads "0.9 FTE, 12-hour nights, every other weekend, holiday rotation." What does the last phrase commit you to?
choices: Working every holiday in the first year
Working roughly half the holidays in a year
No holidays, because night shift is exempt
Holidays only if the department is short-staffed
quiz.why: Holiday rotation means the holidays are shared across the staff, working out to about half of them a year. Night shift carries no exemption, and holiday coverage is scheduled in advance rather than triggered by short staffing. Working every holiday would be written as a holiday requirement, not a rotation.

quiz.q: Two postings differ only in scheduling language: one says self-scheduling, the other says block scheduling. What is the practical difference?
choices: Self-scheduling lets you request your own shifts inside rules before the schedule is built; block scheduling is a fixed repeating pattern
Self-scheduling means you can decline any shift after the schedule posts
Block scheduling means you choose a block of vacation each quarter
Self-scheduling applies only to per diem staff
quiz.why: Self-scheduling is a request process bounded by rules on weekends and nights, and it is worth real quality of life. Block scheduling means the same repeating pattern every cycle. Neither term lets you decline posted shifts, block scheduling is not about vacation, and self-scheduling is common for full-time staff.

quiz.q: A per diem posting lists a base of `$30.00` an hour against a full-time line at `$21.50`. For a first hospital job, what is the strongest argument against the per diem role?
choices: Per diem rates are usually withdrawn after 90 days
Per diem staff cannot be scheduled on nights
Per diem carries a written minimum commitment
Per diem gives the fewest training hours and the least protection, and no benefits, which is exactly what a new tech needs most
quiz.why: The higher rate compensates for no benefits, minimal orientation, and little job protection, and a brand-new tech needs training hours more than an extra nine dollars an hour. The rate is not withdrawn at 90 days, per diem staff frequently work nights, and the minimum commitment, commonly two shifts a month plus a holiday, is a small obligation rather than the real drawback.

quiz.q: A candidate reads a posting requiring "1 year of patient care experience preferred" and does not apply because he has none. What is the error?
choices: None; preferred experience is functionally required at hospitals
Preferred is not required, and experience minimums are routinely waived for a certified EMT, so not applying is the cheapest mistake available
He should apply only after calling the recruiter for permission
He should apply and state that he has one year of experience, since EMT class counts
quiz.why: Preferred means the screener would like it, not that the software rejects you, and EMT certification frequently satisfies the intent of a patient care minimum. Reading yourself out of a posting is the most common self-inflicted loss. You do not need permission to apply, and inflating experience is a verification failure that ends the application.

quiz.q: A union posting lists a published step scale. What should the candidate expect?
choices: Pay set by years of service, a defined probationary period, seniority rules for shift bids and time off, and dues from the check
Full freedom to negotiate the hourly rate, since the scale is only a guideline
No probationary period, because union protection starts on day one
Automatic assignment to day shift as the senior line
quiz.why: A step scale ties the rate to years of service, and union contracts also define the probationary period, seniority rules for bidding shifts and time off, and dues. The rate itself is barely negotiable, although the starting step sometimes is. Probation still exists and is defined explicitly, and new staff bid last, so days are usually the least available line.

quiz.q: An applicant compares `$23.00` base days against `$21.00` base nights with a `$4.00` night differential, working every other weekend with a `$2.50` weekend differential. What is the correct way to decide?
choices: Take the higher posted base, because differentials are not guaranteed
Compare annual salary estimates published on job boards
Compare the effective rate for the shifts actually worked, since the night line runs `$25.00` on weekdays and `$27.50` on weekend nights
Take the day line, because differentials stop after orientation
quiz.why: Differentials stack onto the base for the hours worked, so the night offer is `$25.00` most shifts and `$27.50` on weekend nights, well above the `$23.00` day line. Posted base alone is the wrong comparison. Differentials are contractual for the shift worked, not bonuses, and they do not end after orientation. Board-published salary estimates are not this employer's numbers.

quiz.q: A hospital portal converts every uploaded resume to plain text before matching it to the posting. Which formatting choice is most likely to cause silent loss of information?
choices: A 10-point common font
Reverse chronological ordering with month and year
Section names Certifications, Experience, Education, Skills
Contact information placed in the document header
quiz.why: Many parsers discard header and footer regions entirely, so a phone number and email living there can vanish without any error shown. A 10-point common font, reverse chronological dates, and standard section names are all exactly what the parser expects.

quiz.q: Where do certifications belong on a first hospital resume, and in what form?
choices: At the top, above Experience, with expiration dates, for example NJ EMT-B, cert number, exp 03/2029
At the bottom, after Education, so experience leads
Inside the objective statement as a single sentence
Only in the cover letter, to keep the resume to one page
quiz.why: Certifications with expiration dates are the exact line a screener hunts for in a 15-second read, so they lead. Burying them under Education costs you that scan. There should be no objective statement at all, and a cover letter is optional and often not read, so credentials cannot live only there.

quiz.q: Which bullet best translates three years of restaurant shift-lead work for an ED tech application?
choices: Worked in a fast-paced environment and wore many hats
Responsible for customer satisfaction and team morale
Trained and onboarded 14 new employees; wrote the shift checklist still in use
Excellent communication skills and a strong work ethic under pressure
quiz.why: The winning bullet is an action verb, a specific task, a number, and a result that outlived you, and training new staff maps directly onto precepting. The other three are adjectives without evidence, which a screener reads past. Every bullet gets a number, because unnumbered claims are invisible.

quiz.q: A candidate opens his resume with "Objective: seeking a challenging position in healthcare where I can grow and make a difference." What should replace it?
choices: A photo and a skills rating graphic
Either two lines of specific summary or the Certifications section itself
A line reading references available upon request
A list of hobbies that show teamwork
quiz.why: The top of page one is your best real estate, so it goes to concrete credentials or two specific summary lines. An objective statement tells a manager nothing. References upon request is assumed and wastes a line, photos and graphics break the parser, and hobbies do not answer the screener's question.

quiz.q: The portal offers a free-text cover letter field for a specific requisition. What is the best use of it?
choices: Paste the resume text so the keywords appear twice
Skip it, since cover letters are never read
Submit a general healthcare letter saved from earlier applications
Four short paragraphs: the role and requisition number, why emergency medicine specifically, two concrete transferable things from your history, and one sentence on availability
quiz.why: Write a letter only when a field exists, and make it specific enough that it could not have been sent anywhere else, which means naming the department and the requisition. A recycled general letter reads as spam because it is one. Duplicating resume text adds nothing, and skipping an offered field wastes a free chance to say why the ED.

quiz.q: A candidate has never placed a urinary catheter but knows the steps from EMT class and adds "urinary catheterization" to the Skills section. What is the consequence?
choices: Skills sections are not verified, so there is no risk
It is acceptable if the interview clarifies it
Clinical skill claims are routinely verified, and a false one ends the application permanently
It is acceptable because catheterization will be taught during orientation anyway
quiz.why: Verification of clinical skills is routine, and a claim you cannot back is treated as dishonesty rather than enthusiasm, which ends the application. Knowing the steps is not sign-off. Being taught it later does not make the present claim true, and correcting it mid-interview does not undo a signed application.

quiz.q: A recruiter calls for a 10 to 20 minute phone screen. Which preparation matters most before answering?
choices: Have your calendar and a pay range ready, along with your certifications and a one-sentence reason for the ED
Have three STAR stories memorized word for word
Have a list of salary data from other states
Have your references on the line for a conference call
quiz.why: The phone screen covers availability, certifications, pay expectation, and why the ED, so the calendar and a range are what you actually need in hand. Full STAR stories belong to the panel interview. Out-of-state salary data does not apply to this market, and references are contacted after the interview, never during a screen.

quiz.q: During an unpaid 3-hour shadow shift, the department gets busy. Which behavior is correct?
choices: Help by taking vital signs so the crew sees you are useful
Stay out of the doorway, keep your hands off equipment, ask questions in the lulls, and learn three people's names
Wait in the break room until the department slows down
Follow the trauma team into the resuscitation bay for the best view
quiz.why: A shadow is observation only with no patient contact, and it is graded even though nobody says so, because the manager asks the staff about you afterward. Touching a patient or equipment is outside what the visit permits. Hiding in the break room forfeits the whole point, and crowding a resuscitation bay is exactly the impression you do not want.

quiz.q: A candidate interviewed 10 days ago, was told a decision would come in a week, and followed up on day 10. It is now day 17 with no answer. What is the best move?
choices: Send a second follow-up now and a third next week
Call the manager's unit directly and ask to speak with her
Stop following up on this requisition and apply to other postings in the same system, which is expected
Withdraw the application so the system knows you are serious
quiz.why: One follow-up after the stated timeline is professional, and further nudges read as anxiety without moving a requisition. Silence is usually structural, because internal candidates and union members often hold bidding rights that must be exhausted first. Calling the clinical unit is an intrusion, and withdrawing simply removes you from consideration.

quiz.q: A written offer arrives by email. Which set of items must be confirmed in it before resigning anything?
choices: Title, FTE, base rate, shift, differentials, start date, orientation length, benefits start date, and any sign-on payback clause
Base rate and start date only, since the rest is standard
The recruiter's name and the requisition number
The union local and the dues rate
quiz.why: The offer letter is the only document that binds, so every term that shapes income and schedule belongs in it, including the benefits start date and any bonus repayment obligation. Rate and date alone leave the shift and differentials undefined. Recruiter details and union dues are real but do not determine what you were hired to do or for how much.

quiz.q: A candidate accepted a written offer and is planning his exit from a retail job he has held for four years. Which action protects him most three years from now?
choices: Using the exit interview to document everything wrong with the store
Telling trusted coworkers first so the news does not surprise them
Dropping the last two scheduled weekend shifts since he is leaving anyway
Recording his manager's personal email and cell number and getting an explicit yes to being a reference
quiz.why: PA programs and hospitals verify employment history years later, and managers move, so personal contact details plus a recorded yes are what make that reference reachable. An exit interview has nothing to win and a reference to lose. Telling coworkers before the manager damages the relationship, and abandoning committed shifts is exactly what a reference remembers.

quiz.q: An applicant gets a verbal offer Monday and a start date three weeks out, then gives two weeks notice Tuesday. On Thursday the background check turns up an unverifiable employment date and the offer is rescinded. What principle was violated?
choices: Nothing is real until the written offer is in hand and the contingencies are cleared, so notice comes after that
Notice must always be four weeks in healthcare
Verbal offers are binding, so the hospital acted improperly
Background checks cannot consider employment dates
quiz.why: Verbal offers die at drug screens and background checks, which is precisely why notice waits for the written offer and cleared contingencies. Two weeks is the standard notice, longer only if you supervise people or hold keys. A contingent verbal offer is not binding, and verifying dates on jobs you listed is a normal part of the check.

quiz.q: In a STAR answer, which section should consume three to four sentences while the others take one each?
choices: Situation
Action, described step by step in the first person
Task
Result
quiz.why: The panel is buying your behavior, so the Action is where the detail goes, described as I rather than we so your part is unmistakable. Situation and Task are one sentence each of context, and the Result is one sentence carrying a number or concrete outcome. Front-loading context is what pushes an answer past 90 seconds.

quiz.q: Asked "tell me about a mistake you made," a candidate says he cannot think of one because he is careful. What is the problem?
choices: It is fine, because admitting errors raises safety concerns
He should have described someone else's mistake instead
Refusing to name one is the actual failure, because the question is testing whether you report and correct errors
He should have named a mistake with the highest possible stakes to show honesty
quiz.why: The panel is testing error behavior, which is the single most important safety trait in a new tech, so having no answer is the failing answer. Pick a real, small-stakes mistake, own it flatly, and spend the answer on what you did immediately, who you told, and what changed. Describing a coworker's mistake dodges the question, and a catastrophic example is unnecessary risk.

quiz.q: Which prioritization answer would a panel score highest for an ED tech?
choices: I do whatever the nurse asks first, in the order she asks
Life threats first, then time-critical items like an EKG within 10 minutes for chest pain or sepsis labs, then by who has waited longest, and I tell the nurse out loud what I am not going to get to
I work fastest tasks first so the list gets shorter
I stay calm and multitask until everything is done
quiz.why: The strong answer states a rule, includes real time-critical numbers, and ends with the sentence that makes it safe: naming out loud what will not get done. Taking tasks purely in the order asked ignores acuity. Shortest-first optimizes your list rather than the patient, and multitasking calmly is a feeling, not a method.

quiz.q: A busy nurse asks the tech to push an IV antiemetic during the interview scenario question. Which answer has the correct three-part structure?
choices: I would do it once, since she is responsible for the order
I would tell her that is not my job and go back to my assignment
I would report her to the charge nurse for asking
I would tell her I am not signed off on that, ask what she needs to happen, offer what I can do, and find someone who can do the rest
quiz.why: The structure is decline the task, keep the relationship, solve her problem, and the last choice does all three. Performing it anyway is outside scope regardless of who wrote the order. A flat refusal preserves the rule but abandons the patient's need. Escalating a routine request to the charge nurse first is disproportionate and damages the working relationship.

quiz.q: Asked "why the ED," which answer is strongest?
choices: Undifferentiated patients, worst-first reasoning, the pace, and the fact that the tech is the hands on almost every early task
I like helping people and I work well under pressure
The night differentials make it the best-paying tech role available
It is the fastest way to accumulate hours for a PA application
quiz.why: The answer should be about the work itself, and naming undifferentiated patients, worst-first thinking, and the tech's role in early tasks shows you understand what the department actually does. Helping people is the answer everyone gives. Pay and hour accumulation are true motivations but describe what the job does for you, not why this work.

quiz.q: Rather than memorizing answers to the roughly twenty-five questions panels ask, what preparation is more efficient?
choices: Write out full answers to all twenty-five and rehearse them nightly

Prepare six stories, because interviewers re-slice the same material: an angry person calmed, a mistake fixed, someone taught, a moment of competing priorities, a disagreement with a supervisor, and doing more than required
Prepare one long biography that covers everything
Prepare nothing, so the answers sound natural
quiz.why: Six well-built stories map onto nearly every behavioral question because panels ask about the same underlying behaviors in different wording. Memorizing twenty-five answers produces recitation and still leaves gaps. A biography answers no behavioral question, and improvising loses the STAR structure and the numbers.

quiz.q: A panel ends with "what questions do you have for us," and the candidate says everything has been covered. How is that scored?
choices: As efficient, since the panel is behind schedule
As neutral, because the questions are a courtesy
As low interest, because your questions are part of the evaluation
As confident, because it signals you already know the role
quiz.why: The closing questions are scored like every other part of the interview, so having none reads as low interest. Bring six written down, ask four or five, and take notes on the answers. Respecting the panel's time does not require giving up your own evaluation of them, and assuming you know the role is not confidence to a hiring manager.

quiz.q: Which closing question most directly shapes how the candidate handles the following two weeks?
choices: What are the next steps, and when do you expect to decide
Does the system offer tuition reimbursement
What is the biggest change the department is going through right now
Is there a path to cross-train into triage or fast track
quiz.why: The next-steps question produces the timeline that controls when you follow up, which is why it is not optional. Tuition reimbursement, department changes, and cross-training are all good questions about the job, but none of them tells you when a single follow-up becomes appropriate and when to stop.

quiz.q: A candidate plans to wear clean scrubs to a panel interview because it is a clinical role. What is the correct guidance?
choices: Scrubs are correct for any hospital interview
Business casual unless you were specifically told to wear scrubs for a shadow shift: collared shirt, clean slacks, closed shoes, a belt
A full suit is required, and anything less is read as casual
Wear whatever you own as long as tattoos are covered
quiz.why: Business casual is the standard for the interview itself; scrubs are correct only when you were told to wear them for a shadow shift. A tie is optional and never wrong, but a full suit is not required. Covering tattoos is sensible on a first interview, yet it does not substitute for dressing for the meeting.

quiz.q: A candidate arrives at a large medical campus garage at 1:48 p.m. for a 2 p.m. interview. What is the realistic outcome and the rule that prevents it?
choices: He arrives comfortably early; 12 minutes is the standard buffer
He should have arrived at 1:15 p.m., because earlier than 45 minutes is the rule
He arrives on time, since hospitals expect interview candidates to be delayed
He risks arriving late or flustered; add 20 minutes for the garage and the walk, be at the building 15 minutes early and at the desk 5 to 10 minutes early
quiz.why: Hospital parking and the walk to the department routinely eat 20 minutes, so 12 minutes leaves no margin and produces a rushed, sweating arrival. The rule is at the building 15 minutes early and at the desk 5 to 10 minutes early. Arriving more than 15 minutes early is its own small imposition, and no interviewer budgets for a candidate's delay.

quiz.q: A strong candidate is abrupt with the security officer at the entrance and with the unit secretary who walks him back. Why does this frequently cost the job?
choices: Security reports every interaction to human resources by policy
Managers routinely ask staff about candidates afterward, so the interview effectively starts in the parking lot
Non-clinical staff sit on the hiring panel at most hospitals
It violates the scent-free and conduct policy applicants sign
quiz.why: Hiring managers ask the people who saw you before and after the panel, which is why the interview starts in the lot and candidates never see this coming. There is no automatic security reporting policy, non-clinical staff are not usually panel members, and no conduct policy governs a visitor who has not been hired.

quiz.q: Orientation at a community ED runs hospital classroom days, department orientation, and then precepted shifts. What is the defining feature of the precepted period?
choices: It is observation only, with no patient contact until it ends
It lasts exactly 90 days at every hospital
An experienced tech signs off each line of a competency checklist, and you cannot perform a skill solo until that line is signed
It replaces the requirement for BLS certification
quiz.why: Precepted shifts, commonly 4 to 8 weeks or 6 to 12 shifts, exist to get the competency checklist signed skill by skill, and each signature is what unlocks solo practice of that skill. You do have patient contact, with the preceptor alongside. Length varies by hospital, and nothing in orientation replaces a BLS card.

quiz.q: A tech finishes a 12-lead at `2106` on the chest pain patient in room 12 and places it on the rack. What still has to happen?
choices: Nothing further; the EKG is on the rack where the provider looks
Chart it at the end of shift with the other tasks
Tell the patient the result so the family stops asking
Close the loop out loud to the nurse or provider: the EKG is done, the time, where it is, and the rate you saw
quiz.why: A task nobody knows you finished is a task you did not do, and a chest pain EKG is time-critical, so it is announced with what you did and when. Leaving it on a rack assumes someone looks. Charting from memory at the end of shift loses the real time. A tech does not interpret or deliver results to the patient.

quiz.q: Which habit is the single fastest way for a new tech to build a reputation in the first two weeks?
choices: Restocking and cleaning without being asked, and answering call lights that are not your patient's
Volunteering for the most difficult procedures on day one
Staying late to finish charting after every shift
Asking the manager weekly for feedback
quiz.why: Restocking, cleaning, and never saying not my patient are noticed within two weeks and cost nothing clinically, which is why they are the fastest reputation available in a hospital. Chasing hard procedures before sign-off is the opposite of trustworthy. Staying late to chart signals you charted from memory. Feedback is worth asking for, but once at 30 days rather than weekly.

quiz.q: A patient's daughter asks the tech when the doctor is coming. Which reply is correct?
choices: The doctor will be right in
I will let your nurse know you are waiting
There are three patients ahead of you, so about an hour
I have no idea, you would have to ask someone else
quiz.why: Telling the nurse is a promise you can keep and it routes the question to the person who can answer it. Right in is an over-promise you do not control and it is remembered when it turns out to be an hour. Inventing a wait time is the same error with a number attached, and a flat brush-off leaves a frightened family with nothing.

quiz.q: A tech misses a scheduled 15-minute restraint check and realizes it 40 minutes later. What is the correct sequence?
choices: Chart the check as though it had been done on time to avoid a gap in the record
Complete the check now and say nothing, since the patient is unharmed
Wait until the end of shift and tell the oncoming tech
Tell the nurse immediately, address the patient's safety, chart factually with real times, and complete the incident or safety report
quiz.why: The response to any error is fixed: report at once, make the patient safe, document objectively with true times, and file the safety report, which is a quality document kept separate from the medical record. Charting a check that did not happen is falsification. Silence and end-of-shift disclosure both add the delay and concealment that actually end jobs.

quiz.q: A new tech is unsure how to set up a suture tray and does not want to look inexperienced in front of the nurse. What is the right move?
choices: Say I do not know, let me find out, then find the answer and come back with it
Set it up from memory and let the provider correct anything wrong
Quietly skip the task and hope another tech picks it up
Look it up on a personal phone at the bedside
quiz.why: Admitting a gap and closing it has never ended a career, while guessing to avoid looking new is one of the standard new-tech mistakes. Improvising a sterile setup wastes supplies and delays care. Dropping a task silently breaks the trust the whole role runs on, and personal phone use where patients and families can see it is its own problem.

quiz.q: A tech works three twelve-hour shifts a week at `$21.00` base with a `$4.00` night differential, and one of the three falls on a weekend night carrying an additional `$2.50`. What does the weekend night shift gross before tax?
quiz.why: The differentials stack: `$21.00` plus `$4.00` plus `$2.50` equals `$27.50` an hour, and 12 hours gives `$330.00`. `$252.00` uses base alone, `$300.00` applies only the night differential, and `$378.00` would require a rate of `$31.50`, higher than any of the stated components add to.

quiz.q: A candidate holding EMT certification and an NHA CPT certificate receives an offer at a union hospital with a published step scale. What is the realistic negotiation?
choices: Ask twice for a higher hourly rate, since persistence signals value
Ask once whether the certifications support starting at the next step, then accept the answer
Decline the offer and ask the recruiter to repost at a higher rate
Negotiate the step scale itself with the union representative
quiz.why: You cannot talk your way up a published grid, but where you start on it is sometimes adjustable for certifications or prior patient-facing work, so one polite ask with a reason attached is the move. A second ask becomes a problem. Requisitions are not reposted at a candidate's request, and the scale is set by contract, not negotiated individually.

quiz.q: A tech coming off `1900` to `0700` intends to sleep at `0830`. By which time should the last caffeine be taken?
choices: `0400`, allowing about two half-lives before sleep
`0600`, since the drive home clears it
`0230` or earlier, about 6 hours before the planned sleep
Any time before the end of shift, since caffeine does not affect trained night workers
quiz.why: Caffeine has a half-life near 5 hours, so the last dose goes at least 6 hours before the planned sleep, which means `0230` for an `0830` bedtime. `0400` leaves only about four and a half hours, and a `0600` coffee is still half present at sleep. Tolerance changes how alert you feel, not how quickly the drug clears.

quiz.q: Which set of habits best supports daytime sleep for a fixed night line?
choices: Blackout curtains, earplugs, a fixed sleep window such as `0830` to `1530` every workday, sunglasses on the drive home, and about 4 hours of anchor sleep at the same clock time on days off
Sleeping whenever you feel tired, with a hard workout right after each shift
Full daytime schedule flipping on every day off to stay social
A heavy meal at `0400` and bright light only in the last hour of the shift
quiz.why: Daytime sleep survives only when it is scheduled and protected, which is what darkness, quiet, a fixed window, sunglasses to blunt morning light, and an anchor block on days off accomplish. Exercising at `0730` fights the sleep you need at `0830`. Flipping fully on days off resets the rhythm, and a heavy `0400` meal plus late bright light makes both the shift and the sleep worse.

quiz.q: Ten months into night shift a tech dreads the drive in, feels flat at home, and needs alcohol to fall asleep. What is the appropriate response?
choices: Treat it as normal adjustment and wait it out until the one-year mark
Request a transfer out of the emergency department immediately
Increase caffeine during shifts and add a sleep aid on days off
Use the department debrief if one is offered and contact the employee assistance program, which is free, confidential, and not part of the personnel file
quiz.why: These are the honest signals of cumulative emotional load, which builds quietly over months rather than after one dramatic case, and EAP exists exactly for this and does not enter the personnel file. Waiting it out lets it deepen. Stimulants and sleep aids treat the surface. A transfer may eventually be reasonable, and internal moves after a year are routine, but it is not the first step.

quiz.q: A PA applicant logs 2,200 hours as an ED tech and 900 hours as a unit clerk. How do most programs classify them?
choices: 2,200 hours of patient care experience and 900 hours of healthcare experience
3,100 hours of patient care experience
2,200 hours of healthcare experience and 900 hours of shadowing
Neither counts without a clinical license
quiz.why: Patient care experience means hands-on responsibility for part of a patient's care, which the tech role clearly is, while a unit clerk works in healthcare without that direct role and counts as healthcare experience. The two are not added together. Clerk hours are employment, not shadowing, and no license is required for either category.

quiz.q: A tech is two years from applying and wants the strongest application built from inside the job. Which combination does the most?
choices: Picking up maximum overtime to push total hours as high as possible
Getting on the code team, cross-training into triage and fast track, becoming fast and clean on the 12-lead, and asking to precept new techs
Transferring to a scribe role to be closer to providers
Working only night shift so days are free for classes
quiz.why: Those four make you useful in ways that generate both skill and the kind of letter that describes leadership rather than attendance. Raw overtime hours pass a floor that most programs set between `500` and `2,000` and stop helping. Scribe work converts direct patient care into healthcare experience, a downgrade. Night shift may be practical but builds nothing by itself.

quiz.q: A tech working three twelve-hour night shifts a week plans prerequisites. Which schedule is sensible?
choices: Four courses in one semester to finish in a single year
Anatomy and physiology with an `0800` lab on a post-night morning
One or two courses per semester, scheduled away from post-shift mornings
No courses until leaving the tech job entirely
quiz.why: One or two courses alongside three twelves is normal and sustainable, and it protects the grade, which is what matters, since a withdrawal or a C in anatomy hurts more than a slower schedule. Four courses on nights ends in a withdrawal. An `0800` lab after a night shift is the classic bad pairing. Quitting the job stops the patient care hours the application needs.

quiz.q: CASPA opens in late April and most target programs use rolling admissions. What follows for an applicant who is otherwise ready?
choices: Submit in the first six weeks, because an identical application sent in September competes for fewer remaining seats
Submit in September, since late applications receive fresher review
Submit only after the final prerequisite grade posts in December
Timing is irrelevant because all applications are reviewed together after the deadline
quiz.why: Rolling admissions means seats fill as interviews happen, so the same application is genuinely stronger in May than in September. Late review is not fresher, it is competing for what is left. Waiting on a December grade forfeits most of the cycle, and a single common review date is what rolling admissions is not.
